transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-10
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jon Clarke (Redwood CSM); Dr. Sara Lee (BeaconMed CMO), Tom Ruiz (BeaconMed CTO), Linda Park (BeaconMed Head of Data), Marcus Hill (BeaconMed DevOps)

Summary: kickoff to onboard BeaconMed onto Redwood inference platform, scope out sandbox > pilot > production path, confirm security and network steps, agree on next steps and owners.

[00:00] Alex: ok, hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with me is Priya our solution engineer and Jon who'll be your CSM, hows everyone doing?
[00:10] Dr. Sara: good thanks, excited to get started, we had a lot of internal interest for the triage assistant so hoping we can move quick
[00:18] Tom: yeah hi all, i'm Tom, CTO, main things for us are latency and PII handling, we need to understand how Redwood treats PHI and what options exist for private deploys
[00:29] Alex: totally, that's exactly what we'll cover — plan is sandbox first (hosted), then pilot on Dedicated GPUs if numbers look good, and then we can discuss Private/VPC on prem if you need air-gap. Priya will walk through the technical bits.
[00:45] Priya: hey, quick note, transcription might have some errors in the meeting notes later, but i'll go over network reqs — for sandbox we only need API key + allowlist, for Dedicated/pilot we recommend VPC peering or private link and we support KMS integrations for envelope encryption
[01:05] Marcus: when you say KMS, is that customer-managed? we need HSM or CMKs in our AWS account ideally
[01:10] Priya: yes, we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS, and if you need HSM-grade we can discuss an enterprise add-on; for the pilot we usually suggest customer CMK so audit trails map to you
[01:25] Tom: and data residency — all inference logs, do they leave region? we prefer EU region for a subset of data, but primary is US-east for most workloads
[01:33] Alex: you can pin regions, Redwood hosted has region selection; logs and audit trails can be configured to remain in region for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we have retention settings and opt-in advanced logging that you can toggle.
[01:48] Linda: on retention, we have strict retention for conversation logs, also we need SSO/SAML to provision access to our team
[01:55] Jon: yep SAML/SCIM is supported, we can help with the SSO setup, i'll own the cutover with your identity team
[02:05] Dr. Sara: great. Priya, can you run through the sample architecture for integrating the triage assistant into our existing portal?
[02:12] Priya: sure, high level: user enters symptom data -> front-end calls your backend -> backend calls Redwood API (text-generation or chat endpoint) -> we return structured JSON back (intent, suggested actions) -> you persist and surface in UI. For high throughput we recommend batching and prefix caching; for low latency interactive flows use the streaming responses.
[02:38] Tom: how does prefix caching work? our concern is both latency and token costs
[02:43] Priya: we do KV cache for common prefixes and can cache embeddings for similarity lookups; caching reduces tokens for repeated prompts and lowers cost while keeping latency low. We'll provide suggested cache TTLs based on your query patterns.
[02:58] Linda: sample question — if we send PHI, is it redacted on Redwood side or should we pre-redact?
[03:05] Alex: recommended approach is client-side redaction for PHI before hitting hosted APIs, but for Dedicated/Private you can keep full text in your VPC and we can disable retention. We'll share the data handling policy doc.
[03:20] Marcus: network — what IP ranges to allow? we run strict egress rules
[03:24] Priya: i'll put the IP ranges in the network guide, but for sandbox it's just a small set of endpoints; for Dedicated we do VPC peering, so you allow peering and security groups; i'll also include ALB/ELB guidance, and port lists.
[03:38] Tom: any upfront benchmarking we should expect? we want to know tokens per second and p99 latency for 512 token prompts
[03:46] Priya: we can run an initial benchmark — typical for our curated models p95 is under 200-300ms on Dedicated for short prompts, but i'll validate with your payloads. we'll do a 1k request run to get throughput numbers.
[04:02] Dr. Sara: timeline — we want pilot in 3 weeks, is that reasonable?
[04:07] Alex: yes, sandbox this week, benchmark next week, Dedicated pilot kickoff two weeks after that — three weeks to pilot start is feasible if we get the samples and firewall work done.
[04:18] Linda: onboarding checklist — SDKs, sample code, swagger, do you provide python/js examples?
[04:23] Priya: yes we have sample SDKs, quickstart repos, and a Postman collection, and we'll share a small integration starter that shows streaming and tool calling.
[04:35] Marcus: question on authentication — token rotation? we need short-lived creds and audit logs
[04:40] Alex: we support short-lived tokens via our auth service and full audit logging; for Dedicated/Private you can route through your identity provider and have SCIM provisioning.
[04:50] Tom: security reviews — we'll need SOC2 report and penetration test results
[04:54] Alex: we'll send the SOC2 report, pen-test summary, and our network diagram in the follow-up.
[05:03] Dr. Sara: success criteria for pilot — what should we measure?
[05:07] Priya: typical metrics: p95 latency, throughput at your expected concurrency, cost per 1k tokens, and accuracy/quality regressions on a fixed eval set. if you have labeled prompts we can run quality baselines.
[05:23] Linda: we have 500 test prompts from our triage flows, can we run those in the sandbox?
[05:28] Priya: absolutely — please share a PHI-free sample dataset and we'll run the baseline.
[05:33] Marcus: anything else on networking — do you require egress to S3 for model caching?
[05:39] Priya: not for hosted, but for Dedicated we do model artifacts and caching in the cluster; we can mirror artifacts into your account in Private deployments. i'll document the artifact flows.
[05:52] Tom: pricing — Alex, can you summarize pilot pricing for Dedicated vs hosted?
[05:56] Alex: short version: hosted is pay-as-you-go per token with some burst limits; Dedicated is a committed capacity monthly with lower per-token unit cost and predictable latency; i'll send a pricing sheet with examples mapped to your expected qps.
[06:09] Dr. Sara: ok great. any blockers?
[06:12] Marcus: need the IP list and peering steps, and i'll coordinate with network next week
[06:16] Linda: i'll prepare PHI-free sample set and share by monday
[06:20] Alex: perfect — i'll follow up with docs, SOC2, and a proposed timeline and calendar invites; Jon will reach out on SSO details.
[06:28] Jon: i'll set up the SAML onboarding thread and include steps for SCIM groups mapping and role-based access.
[06:34] Dr. Sara: thanks, quick Q — any red flags for us choosing Redwood vs competitor X?
[06:39] Alex: main differentiators we've seen are production-focused tooling (tracing, token-level cost breakdowns) and the unified runtime that makes Dedicated/Private transitions easier. competitors may have simpler hosted apis but less control over deployment.
[06:56] Tom: sounds good, excited to see the benchmark numbers.
[07:00] Alex: ok we'll run the benchmark and sync next week, thanks everyone.

End transcript. Notes: some speaker labels auto-generated may mismatch in final export; some product names transcribed as 'redwoodded' or 'KV cash' in early drafts, we'll clean up internally.
